title: ConversationState
description: Compact structured context carried across turns in one session, so a follow-up like 'and the fee?' can be resolved without re-parsing the whole conversation as text (Section 3, principle 7; Section 9).

session_id.description: Unique identifier for this conversation session.

last_resolved_procedure_id.description: The most recently resolved procedure_id, used to interpret a follow-up that doesn't re-name the procedure. Null if nothing has been resolved yet, or explicitly cleared on a topic switch (Section 9).

last_requested_section_types.description: Which fields were asked about most recently, for the same reason as last_resolved_procedure_id.

active_filters.description: Filters currently carried forward across turns (e.g. a jurisdiction or effective date the user set earlier in the conversation).

unresolved_references.description: Follow-up phrases the interpretation step could not yet resolve against last_resolved_procedure_id (e.g. an ambiguous pronoun), kept so the next turn can retry.

recent_raw_turns.description: Optional, capped rolling buffer of the last few raw user messages (verbatim, unsegmented). Not consulted by default interpretation — the structured fields above (last_resolved_procedure_id, last_requested_section_types, active_filters) remain the primary and preferred path. This exists only as a fallback for Query Interpretation to consult when those structured fields fail to resolve a follow-up reference. The cap at 3 is deliberate: this must never grow into a full transcript, or it reintroduces the non-deterministic 'let the model re-read everything' problem this design was built to avoid (Section 3, principle 2).

updated_at.description: Timestamp this state was last modified. On a detected procedure switch or explicit correction, last_resolved_procedure_id and last_requested_section_types must be reset rather than left stale (Section 9).
